questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have lived i Canada before, and wanted to come back and experience it. Exchange gave me that opportunity

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Going on exchange was one of the best decissions i have ever made

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The go global setup at UBC was quite extensive an helped with any questions

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Some appartments or houses

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a kitchen - Shared four people

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is very cosy and recommendable. The house it self was not of high standards. You had to buy everything for the kitchen (pans, utencils, plates). It was completely empty when we arrived. You also had to buy your own internet cable since that was not part of the house. I would recommend just bying a big enough data package on your phone so you can share internet to you computer while staying at your house.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Our sinks clogged the first week, panels where falling off, kitchen cabinet doors where falling of their hiinges and the house wasnt cleen upon arrival

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Easy but time-demanding

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Signing up to courses through their wrokday app worked really well, also changing courses was super easy

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Online support from go global.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register for courses that you want before, but if you want to change course it is not hard at all. It is definately worth it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Had 2 great courses that was held in person and really good professors. Then i had one online course which was great, but motivation was hard to find when doing it online. My last course was just not good. I was not a fan of the professor and found the subject to be an overcomplicatipon of something very very simple.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 300 level courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Depends on what class. One i would highlights had a high level of student inclusiong in lectures which worked great. 
The biggest difference would be the ongoing assignments through the semester and the importance of attendance on your grade

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Politics and development - POLI 338B
Issues in Comparative Politics - POLI333
European Integration - POLI327
Contemporary Political theory - POLI341

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Contemporary Political theory - POLI341. I had the best professor i have ever had. Very good lecture method as well, with a high level of expectation on students whiile also incluging them.

European Integration - POLI327. Our professor was German which made a European Integration course feel more valid when taking it i Canada

questions.answer: Imed and train pass is mandatory - 2500kr when starting at UBC

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food is very expensive in Canada. Alcohol as well, although it is cheaper in bars than in Denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The clubs at UBC are amazing. They create that sense of a student life, and offer some amazing trips.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I went on a surf trip and a skitrip. Also went to a movie premiere on a skifilm

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above. It is a great way to meet other students and bond both with Canadians and other exchange students

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Lots of hikes, Skiing in Whistler, See Granville Island. Go on a roadtrip, visit Vancouver Island.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Quite easy since i have lived here before. But you do have to adjust to the canadian friendlyness and openness. 
We did have som not so pleasent encounters with fentanyl addicts since it is a big problem in downtown Vancouver

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the Clubs and use events as an opportunity to talk with all sorts of different people. Don't just stick to the danish group, but mix with different people

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: We did have som not so pleasent encounters with fentanyl addicts since it is a big problem in downtown Vancouver

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their openness and friendly behavior

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Enjoy it while you can - Time goes by very fast
Socialize through the clubs or other gatherings. It is so great to get friends from all over the world
Enjoy that your courses will all be translated to Paased/ not passed. It is a privelige to get more free time

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many good people and seeing the most beautifull nature in the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding enough time to do everything you want to while also habing an academic life

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
